question: Jefferson Middle School has the same number of boys and girls. Three-fourths of the girls and two-thirds of the boys went on a field trip. What fraction of the students on the field trip were girls?
solution:
Because the school has equally many girls and boys, a twelfth of the girls and a twelfth of the boys represent the same number of students. Write both attendance fractions in twelfths:

\[\frac34=\frac9{12},\qquad \frac23=\frac8{12}.\]

Thus the trip includes 9 equal-sized parts of girls and 8 equal-sized parts of boys. There are \(9+8=17\) such parts altogether, so the fraction of participants who were girls is

\[\boxed{\frac9{17}},\]

choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
